proposals.before: King Cheng inspected the archives, found the Duke of Zhou's prayer document that had been sunk in the river, and wept, saying: 'Who dared say that the Duke of Zhou wished to rebel!'
proposals.after: King Cheng inspected the archives, found the Duke of Zhou's document recording the river offering, and wept, saying: 'Who dared say that the Duke of Zhou wished to rebel!'
proposals.reason: 沈書 refers to the written record of the fingernail-sinking offering, not a document that was itself sunk in the river.

decisions.reason: In the preceding units the Duke of Zhou sinks his fingernails in the river (揃其爪以沈於河) and separately writes and stores that prayer in the archives (書而藏之記府). 沈書 is therefore that archived record of the river offering, not a document that had itself been sunk; the proposed literal correctly removes the invented sinking of the document.
